full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 223

Zhang v. Beijing MouDie Culture Communication Co., Ltd., Cheng, and Ma — dispute over infringement of the right to disseminate works via information networks

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on December 15, 2023)

Keywords
Civil proceedings; infringement of the right to disseminate works via information networks; jurisdiction; place of infringing act

Ruling Gist
The place of infringement results for infringement of the right to disseminate works via information networks is uncertain and should not serve as the basis for determining jurisdiction. When determining jurisdiction in civil disputes over infringement of the right to disseminate works via information networks, Article 15 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Hearing Civil Disputes over Infringement of the Right to Disseminate Works via Information Networks shall apply, i.e., the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place of infringement or the defendant's domicile.

Basic Facts
The plaintiff, Zhang, filed a lawsuit with the Qinhuangdao Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province, the place of his domicile, on the grounds that the defendants, Beijing MouDie Culture Communication Co., Ltd., Cheng, and Ma, had, without authorization, published and used his copyrighted photographic artwork on relevant websites, infringing his right to disseminate the work via information networks. The defendant Ma raised an objection to jurisdiction on the grounds that jurisdiction should be determined pursuant to Article 15 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Hearing Civil Disputes over Infringement of the Right to Disseminate Works via Information Networks (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisions on Information Network Dissemination Rights"), and that Qinhuangdao City is the plaintiff's domicile, not the place of infringement or the defendant's domicile. Ma requested that the case be transferred to the Beijing Internet Court, which is the place of infringement and the defendant's domicile.

Judgment
The Qinhuangdao Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province rendered a civil ruling (2021) Ji 03 Zhi Min Chu No. 27 on June 2, 2021, dismissing Ma's objection to jurisdiction. Ma, dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, filed an appeal. The Hebei High People's Court rendered a civil ruling (2021) Ji Min Xia Zhong No. 66 on August 24, 2021, vacating the first-instance ruling and transferring the case to the Beijing Internet Court for trial. Upon review, the Beijing Internet Court and the Beijing High People's Court concluded that the Hebei High People's Court's transfer of the case to the Beijing Internet Court for trial was improper, and thus reported the matter to the Supreme People's Court for designation of jurisdiction. The Supreme People's Court rendered a civil ruling (2022) Zui Gao Fa Min Xia No. 42 on August 22, 2022, determining that the case shall be tried by the Beijing Internet Court.

Reasoning
The Supreme People's Court held that Article 25 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The place of commission of an information network infringement includes the location of computers and other information equipment used to commit the alleged infringing act, and the place of occurrence of the infringement results includes the domicile of the infringed party." The "information network infringement" referred to in this provision targets infringements against general civil rights committed through information networks. However, the "right to disseminate works via information networks" is a statutory right enjoyed by copyright owners as provided in Article 10, paragraph 1 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, i.e., the right to provide works to the public through wired or wireless means, enabling members of the public to access the works at a time and place of their choosing. Based on the nature and characteristics of the right to disseminate works via information networks, once an act infringing such a right occurs, it results in the public being able to access the work at a time and place of their choosing, and the geographical scope involved in the infringing act is uncertain. Therefore, Article 15 of the Provisions on Information Network Dissemination Rights stipulates: "Civil disputes over infringement of the right to disseminate works via information networks shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place of infringement or the defendant's domicile. The place of infringement includes the location of network servers, computer terminals, and other equipment used to commit the alleged infringing act. If both the place of infringement and the defendant's domicile are difficult to determine or are located outside the territory of China, the location of computer terminals and other equipment where the plaintiff discovers the infringing content may be deemed the place of infringement." Consequently, Article 15 of the Provisions on Information Network Dissemination Rights is a special provision specifically addressing the jurisdiction of civil disputes over infringement of the right to disseminate works via information networks, which is a particular type of civil right. In determining jurisdiction in civil disputes over infringement of the right to disseminate works via information networks, Article 15 of the Provisions on Information Network Dissemination Rights shall serve as the basis.

In this case, Qinhuangdao City is the plaintiff's domicile and does not fall within the "place of infringement" or "defendant's domicile" under Article 15 of the Provisions on Information Network Dissemination Rights. This case also does not involve the exceptional circumstance under Article 15 of the Provisions on Information Network Dissemination Rights that "both the place of infringement and the defendant's domicile are difficult to determine or are located outside the territory of China." Therefore, the Qinhuangdao Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province does not have jurisdiction over this case, and the Hebei High People's Court's transfer of the case to the Beijing Internet Court was not improper.

Relevant Legal Provisions
1. Article 29 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China
2. Articles 24 and 25 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China
3. Article 15 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Hearing Civil Disputes over Infringement of the Right to Disseminate Works via Information Networks
